screens.name: landing
strengths: The oversized serif headline gives the experience a recognizable editorial voice.
The fractured mirror makes the central game metaphor tangible before the first tap.
problems: The mirror loses definition against its lavender glow. Reduce the surrounding bloom and strengthen the frame and shard edges.
The paragraph and CTA footer repeat the card count without clearly explaining the payoff. Replace the footer with 'Genii predicts your final 8. Then you see what it called.'

screens.name: lobby
strengths: Three distinct voice choices make personalization immediately understandable.
The colored orbs introduce Genii's early form through a coherent visual vocabulary.
problems: The entire instruction panel is italic, making supporting copy feel equally emphatic. Keep option titles in serif and set their descriptions in regular sans serif.
The first option looks selected, but there is no explicit indication that tapping advances. Add 'Tap a voice to continue' above the options and reserve the stronger border for an actual selection.

screens.name: chapter intro
strengths: The floating phone island gives the chapter a clear visual identity.
The mirror thumbnail connects answering cards with visible progression.
problems: The hero illustration consumes roughly a third of the screen before the chapter information appears. Reduce its container height by 40–60 CSS pixels and bring the chapter title upward.
The progress panel splits '0 of 40' from 'shards' and adds six tiny card drawings as another counter. Use '0 / 40 shards' on one line and a simple '6 cards in this chapter' beneath it.

screens.name: scenario card
strengths: The family-photo scenario is specific, funny and easy to picture.
Large answer targets and restrained option decoration support quick decisions.
problems: The mirror, global card count and miniature shard strip crowd the header beside the logo. Remove the shard strip from this header and retain the mirror plus card count.
'Skip' and 'Not my life' look like interchangeable secondary actions. Add brief helper text explaining their difference, or give 'Not my life' the clearer label 'Doesn't apply to me.'

screens.name: reply card
strengths: The family chat makes the format feel meaningfully different from a standard questionnaire.
The private-boundary answer is legible and emotionally plausible.
problems: The chat container, incoming bubbles and four outgoing choices create too many nested borders. Remove the outer chat-container border and shadow, keeping only the message bubbles.
'Tap a reply to send it' contradicts the option that texts a parent privately. Change the instruction to 'What would you do?' and remove quotation marks from answer choices.

screens.name: receipts card
strengths: The receipt treatment turns a checklist into a memorable interaction.
Checkboxes, item separators and the total make the multiselect behavior understandable.
problems: The oversized question forces the receipt and submission action into a dense stack. Reduce this question's type size to match the scenario-card heading and tighten its bottom margin.

'Tear it off' has a disabled-looking lavender fill without explaining the requirement. Use a visibly distinct disabled state with 'Choose at least one,' then switch to the primary gradient when an item or 'None of these' is selected.

screens.name: rank card
strengths: Numbered rows and FIRST/LAST labels communicate the ordering task well.
The dice island extends the chapter world without competing with the answer list.
problems: The handle combines dots and arrows into an unfamiliar control. Replace it with a conventional six-dot grip and show separate up/down buttons only when a row is focused.
'Tap in order' is ambiguous because all four rows already have ranks. Change the helper to 'Drag to reorder' and label the confirmation 'Confirm this order.'

screens.name: late-run card
strengths: The fitted-sheet detail delivers one of the strongest comic hooks in the set.
The evolved glass slime makes progression visible while preserving the established card shell.
problems: Genii's expression is tiny and detached from the scenario by the card edge. Increase the eyes slightly and bring the slime closer to the card's upper-right corner.
The large home island beneath the card adds considerable visual weight without advancing the interaction. Reduce its opacity and visible height so the question remains the clear focal point.

screens.name: lock
strengths: The shift to deep violet gives the commitment moment genuine ceremony.
Eight numbered cards surrounding the completed mirror make the prediction mechanic concrete.
problems: The warning panel emphasizes locked chapter answers more strongly than the primary action emphasizes locked guesses. Change the button to 'Lock guesses & play the final 8' and shorten the panel to one sentence.
The numbered prediction cards lack the crisp definition of the mirror frame. Reduce their bloom and strengthen the number contrast so all eight read immediately.

screens.name: two archetypes
strengths: The divided mirror is the strongest visual expression of 'two sides, both you.'
Archetype names have enough scale and contrast to create a rewarding reveal.
problems: The insight plaque overlaps the mirror base and interrupts its silhouette. Move it below the frame with a small, consistent gap.
The low-contrast Next control is stranded far below the reveal. Raise its contrast and use the same fixed bottom navigation position throughout the Stories sequence.

screens.name: your map
strengths: The two groups preserve the people/life structure established by the archetype reveal.
Glass tracks and luminous markers translate the six leans into the brand's material language.
problems: Endpoint pills and centered stat labels compete on the same horizontal line, especially around Blueprint and Compass. Give each stat name its own small row above the endpoint labels.
The bars look draggable even though they report results. Remove slider-like tick marks and reduce the knobs into smaller fixed markers so the display reads as a map.

screens.name: what Genii knows best
strengths: The featured Read the Room card establishes a clear strongest finding.
Several descriptions are specific enough to feel like observations rather than generic personality praise.
problems: Five secondary cards repeat essentially the same gemstone, making the screen feel like a dense inventory. Reduce secondary icon size and use one compact, consistently spaced list beneath the featured card.
Strong versus clear signal depends heavily on subtle gemstone differences explained only at the bottom. Put a small 'Strong' or 'Clear' label directly on each row and remove the remote legend.

screens.name: room by room
strengths: The miniature islands give each life context a distinct and appealing identity.
Contextual descriptions make the abstract stats easier to recognize in everyday behavior.
problems: The archetype pills sit beside headings with inconsistent remaining space. Put each pill in a consistent position beneath its heading or at the card's upper-right corner.
'With money' makes a categorical spending claim from Wanderlust that feels broader than the displayed evidence. Soften it to 'You lean toward spending on a story rather than saving for a someday.'

screens.name: Genii's calls
strengths: The large 5 of 8 provides a satisfying, immediately readable outcome.
The eight-card grid makes successes and surprises inspectable.
problems: Long serif titles, status labels and pills compete inside narrow tiles. Reduce tile-title size, use consistent three-line title areas and align every status footer to the bottom.
'Right side' is unexplained and the half-circle symbol does not clarify it. Rename it 'Side matched' and add a compact legend: 'Called it = exact answer; side matched = same lean.'

screens.name: share card
strengths: The mirror and paired archetypes create a recognizable image worth sharing.
Story/Post and Night/Day controls offer useful choices without overwhelming the main action.
problems: The exported-card preview gives tiny space to the traits and challenge line while repeating large archetype typography. Enlarge those bottom details and reduce the mirror height slightly.
The opposite-archetype paragraph adds another concept beneath an already complete sharing flow. Remove it from this screen and place it inside the friend-challenge destination.

screens.name: get the app
strengths: The lunch-photo-to-island illustration gives the app handoff a concrete visual premise.
The dark App Store action stands out clearly against the bright violet background.
problems: 'Miia lives it' points toward an illustration showing Genii and a mirror, without a visible Miia. Add an existing Miia character asset beside the lunch bowl and move the label to point directly at her.
The lower screen stacks the acquisition CTA with three equally styled links. Keep the friend challenge as the primary secondary action and reduce methodology and data links to a smaller footer.

top_fixes: Rebuild each map-stat header as three rows: stat name, endpoint labels, then track. Remove the decorative ticks and shrink the fixed result markers.
Standardize the Genii's calls tiles with equal-height title areas and bottom-aligned status footers; replace 'Right side' with 'Side matched' and explain the distinction once.
Flatten the reply card by removing the outer chat border and shadow; change its instruction to 'What would you do?' so private actions make sense.
Keep the featured strongest-finding card, then compress the other five findings into uniform rows with explicit Strong/Clear labels.
Add the existing Miia asset to the app illustration and anchor 'Miia lives it' to her rather than the mirror island.
Remove miniature shard strips from active-card headers; keep the evolving mirror and readable card count.
Create one consistent Stories navigation treatment with a visible Next action, clear contrast and a fixed bottom position.
Reduce decorative bloom around the landing mirror and lock-screen prediction cards, preserving sharp frame edges and readable numbers.
hooks: The set holds attention through unusual scenarios, changing interaction formats and the accumulating mirror. The two-archetype reveal is the strongest screenshot moment: it gives the journey a distinctive visual payoff. Strengthen it by moving the insight plaque below the mirror and tightening the space before Next. The middle of the reveal loses momentum through repetitive panels and dense labels; it needs sharper pacing to reach award-level craft.
brand_fit: The violet glass world is cohesive, and the progression from orb to glass slime fits Genii well. The deep violet lock feels like a purposeful expansion of the same world. The main gap is material discipline: bloom, translucent panels and repeated gemstones sometimes obscure hierarchy instead of enriching it. The app handoff also needs a visible Miia to complete the product story.

meta.judge: Codex CLI, read-only, ephemeral, same 16 screens as R3
